title: Local Veteran and University of Lynchburg Graduate Student Shares Story of Healing and Support for Veterans - NewsBreak
text:
4 hours ago Michael Guertin is a U.S. Army Reserve veteran and a graduate student at the University of Lynchburg. He is studying for a Master of Science in Clinical Mental Health Counseling and plans to graduate in 2027. On November 11, 2025, Guertin was the keynote speaker at the University of Lynchburg’s Veterans Day luncheon. His speech, titled 'Reframing Strength: A Veteran’s Journey to Healing and Service,' focused on his 13 years in the Army Reserve. He discussed the discipline and structure of military life, as well as the challenges he faced after service.
Guertin completed three overseas tours, including one in Iraq and two at Guantanamo Bay, Cuba. He received several medals, such as the Army Achievement Medal and the Global War on Terrorism Medal. He stated that he does not consider himself a hero and highlighted the importance of seeking help and support.
Guertin grew up in New York’s Hudson Valley. He said his faith and family values influenced his decision to join the military. After basic training and military police school, he was deployed to Iraq. There, he experienced events that affected his mental health, including crossing a suspected minefield and being near an IED explosion. He reported developing post-traumatic stress disorder, chronic pain, and fatigue due to combat and exposure to burn pits.
After returning home, Guertin found it difficult to process his experiences. He served two more tours at Guantanamo Bay before leaving the military in 2020. He then worked as a project manager. He said that unresolved trauma affected his family life, especially after his first son was born.
Following surgery for back pain, Guertin decided to change careers. With support from his wife, Emma, he began studying mental health counseling. He now shares his experiences to encourage other veterans and community members to seek support.
